key_insight: Optimizing a Cu2NiGeS4 thin-film solar cell with In2S3 as the electron-transport layer and MoTe2 as the hole-transport layer could raise simulated efficiency to 28.44% by improving carrier separation and reducing recombination.
engineering_relevance: This study provides practical design rules for high-efficiency, earth-abundant thin-film photovoltaics by tuning layer thickness, doping, defects, and parasitic losses in a realistic device stack.
method: SCAPS-1D simulation of an In2S3/Cu2NiGeS4/MoTe2 solar-cell architecture
Band alignment, electric-field, carrier-distribution, and recombination analysis
Parametric optimization of thickness, doping, defect density, resistance, temperature, and illumination
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an optimized PCE of 28.44% with VOC = 0.984 V, JSC = 34.39 mA/cm2, and FF = 84.04% under AM1.5G at 300 K, exceeding previously reported 6.25–21.17% values for similar CNGS cells.
watch_item: The result is a computational prediction, so real-device performance may be lower due to fabrication variability, interface quality, and unmodeled material imperfections.
paper_title: Device Engineering and Performance Optimization of Cu2NiGeS4 Thin-Film Solar Cells with In2S3/MoTe2 Charge-Selective Layers: A Computational Study
